ruling_on_oaq6_non_annotation: AGREE that leaving OAQ 6's '13 code-level / 103 comment-or-docstring' split un-annotated was the correct call, not an oversight, and I reach this independently rather than inheriting the coordinator's stated view. The counting-basis annotation pattern used successfully five times this iteration works because in each case a reader can navigate to a complete, internally-verifiable enumeration inside this document and recount it (15 policy-disposition rows, 13 ADR headings, 20 declared C4 nodes, 9 CheckpointManager methods, 4 SS 13a corrections) and get the stated figure. OAQ 6's 13-vs-103 split has no such internal enumeration to point to: the actual 13-item table lives in an external file (path_violations.md) not reproduced in this document, and the entire content of OAQ 6 is a formal declaration that the figure is DISPUTED -- a competing independent measurement (~95/23) exists, uses a different method, and the HLD explicitly states 'Both cannot stand' and refuses to size FR-15 on either number pending an AST re-derivation. Attaching a counting-basis note in the same visual style used for the five genuinely-resolved counts would misrepresent an open empirical dispute as a scoping clarification, which is a regression in honesty dressed as a consistency improvement. The correct treatment of an unverified number is to say so prominently, which OAQ 6 already does throughout, not to give it the same reassuring cross-reference format as a number that has actually been reconciled.
